main.title: Schindler's List
main.summary: Schindler's List reached cinemas in 1993, telling the story of industrialist Oskar Schindler and the more than a thousand mostly Polish Jewish people he saved through employment in his factories.

cards.heading: Schindler's List
cards.text: Schindler's List reached cinemas in 1993, telling the story of industrialist Oskar Schindler and the more than a thousand mostly Polish Jewish people he saved through employment in his factories. Steven Spielberg directed Steven Zaillian's adaptation of Thomas Keneally's Schindler's Ark. Liam Neeson plays Schindler, with Ben Kingsley as accountant Itzhak Stern and Ralph Fiennes as SS officer Amon Göth. Survivor Poldek Pfefferberg had worked for years to bring the story to public attention. Filming in Kraków placed the production close to the locations of the events it portrayed.

main.title: Mandela and de Klerk share the Nobel Peace Prize
main.subtitle: An unfinished transition
main.summary: The 1993 Nobel Peace Prize recognized Nelson Mandela and F. W. de Klerk’s work toward ending apartheid peacefully.

cards.heading: An unfinished transition
cards.text: Nelson Mandela and South African president F. W. de Klerk were jointly announced as Nobel Peace Prize laureates on October 15, 1993. The committee recognised their work towards ending apartheid peacefully and laying the foundations of democratic government. Mandela had left prison in February 1990, and negotiations were moving towards the country's first democratic national election with universal adult suffrage. Political violence and difficult talks continued through the transition; Mandela's election and inauguration followed in 1994.

cards.heading: Channel Tunnel
cards.text:
The Channel Tunnel (French: Tunnel sous la Manche), sometimes referred to as the Chunnel, is a 50.46-kilometre (31.35-mile) railway tunnel beneath the English Channel which connects Folkestone in the United Kingdom with Coquelles in northern France. Opened in 1994, it remains the only fixed link between Great Britain and the European mainland.

The tunnel has the longest underwater section of any tunnel in the world, at 37.9 km (23.5 miles), reaching a depth of 75 m (246 ft) below sea level and runs, on average, 45 m (148 ft) below the seabed. It is the third-longest railway tunnel in the world. Although the tunnel was designed for speeds up to 200 km/h (120 mph), trains are limited to a maximum speed of 160 km/h (99 mph) for safety reasons. It connects to high-speed railway lines on either end: the LGV Nord in France and High Speed 1 in the United Kingdom.

main.title: Nelson Mandela becomes president
main.summary: On 10 May 1994, Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as president of South Africa after the country’s first democratic national election with universal adult suffrage.

cards.heading: Nelson Mandela becomes president
cards.text:
Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as South Africa's president on May 10, 1994, following the country's first democratic national election with universal adult suffrage. The anti-apartheid activist, lawyer, former political prisoner and leader of uMkhonto we Sizwe became the country's first non-white head of state.

Mandela took office at seventy-five and served until June 14, 1999. His age contributed to his decision to leave after one presidential term.

main.title: Pulp Fiction
main.summary: Pulp Fiction is a 1994 American crime film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino from a story he conceived with Roger Avary.

cards.heading: Pulp Fiction
cards.text:
Pulp Fiction is a 1994 American crime film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino from a story he conceived with Roger Avary. It tells four intertwining tales of crime and violence in Los Angeles. The film stars John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Bruce Willis, Tim Roth, Ving Rhames, and Uma Thurman. The title refers to the pulp magazines and hardboiled crime novels popular during the mid-twentieth century, known for their graphic violence and punchy dialogue.

Tarantino wrote Pulp Fiction in 1992 and 1993, incorporating scenes that Avary originally wrote for True Romance (1993). Its plot occurs out of chronological order. The film features self-referential elements, monologues, casual conversations with eclectic dialogue, and an ironic combination of humor and violence. TriStar Pictures turned down the script as "too demented". Miramax Films co-chairman Harvey Weinstein was enthralled, however, and the film became the first that Miramax Films fully financed.

main.title: Rwandan genocide
main.summary: From April to July 1994, Hutu militias systematically murdered Tutsi people across Rwanda, also killing moderate Hutu and Twa.

cards.heading: Rwandan genocide
cards.text: From April to July 1994, Hutu militias systematically murdered Tutsi people across Rwanda, also killing moderate Hutu and Twa. Hundreds of thousands died during roughly one hundred days, and widespread sexual violence accompanied the killings. Neighbours often became perpetrators or victims within the same communities. Long-standing persecution had already driven many Tutsi into exile. Civil war began in 1990 when the Rwandan Patriotic Front entered from Uganda, and the 1993 Arusha Accords brought a tentative peace. The genocide unfolded during that war and devastated the country's population and social life.

main.title: Steven Spielberg’s first competitive Oscars
main.summary: On 21 March 1994, Schindler’s List earned Steven Spielberg his first competitive Oscars, for directing and as one of its Best Picture producers.

cards.heading: Steven Spielberg’s first competitive Oscars
cards.text:
Schindler's List earned Steven Spielberg his first competitive Academy Awards on March 21, 1994: Best Director and Best Picture, the latter shared through his role as one of the film's producers. The recognition marked a new milestone for the filmmaker associated with New Hollywood and the rise of the modern blockbuster.

Born on December 18, 1946, Spielberg went on to receive honours across film, television, theatre and recorded music, including Academy Awards, BAFTAs, Emmys, a Tony and a Grammy. His later lifetime distinctions included the AFI Life Achievement Award in 1995 and the Kennedy Center Honor in 2006.

main.title: Forrest Gump
main.subtitle: One life passes through several decades of American history
main.summary: Robert Zemeckis' Forrest Gump follows a man from Alabama whose life repeatedly intersects with events much larger than himself. Tom Hanks plays Forrest, with Robin Wright as his childhood friend Jenny and Gary Sinise as Lieutenant Dan. Released in the United States on 6 July 1994, the film adapts Winston Groom's novel through a screenplay by Eric Roth.

cards.heading: A story told from a bench
cards.text: Robert Zemeckis' Forrest Gump follows a man from Alabama whose life repeatedly intersects with events much larger than himself. Tom Hanks plays Forrest, with Robin Wright as his childhood friend Jenny and Gary Sinise as Lieutenant Dan. Released in the United States on 6 July 1994, the film adapts Winston Groom's novel through a screenplay by Eric Roth.

cards.heading: Loyalty through changing decades
cards.text: Forrest tells his story to people waiting beside him on a bench. Football, military service in Vietnam, table tennis and a shrimp business become episodes in an account governed by loyalty and persistence. Jenny's life moves through the same decades along a much less secure path. Returning to their relationship gives the film a personal thread through its changes of setting. Forrest's account often leaves the audience to recognise the historical significance of encounters that he describes in straightforward terms.

cards.heading: History inside a personal memory
cards.text: Zemeckis combines this storytelling with visual effects that place Forrest inside familiar historical footage. The technique makes public history part of his apparently ordinary recollection, while other effects support Lieutenant Dan's changing circumstances. Popular recordings establish different periods, and Alan Silvestri's original score supplies a musical continuity across them. The film's sentiment depends especially on the contrast between its spectacular coincidences and Forrest's enduring concern for a small number of people.

main.title: DVD
main.summary: Developed in 1995, DVD brought much greater storage capacity to an optical disc the same size as a CD.

cards.heading: DVD
cards.text: Developed in 1995, DVD brought much greater storage capacity to an optical disc the same size as a CD. The format first reached the Japanese market in November 1996. A single-layer disc held up to 4.7 gigabytes, supporting video, software and other computer data. Factory-produced DVD-ROMs carried fixed content, while recordable and rewritable versions allowed users to create their own discs. The extra capacity helped make DVD a widely used home-video format and a means of distributing large software packages without changing the familiar disc's physical dimensions.

main.title: The .mp3 extension is chosen
main.summary: Fraunhofer researchers adopted .mp3 as the filename extension for MPEG Audio Layer III on July 14, 1995.

cards.heading: A filename becomes a familiar format
cards.text:
Fraunhofer researchers chose .mp3 as the filename extension for MPEG Audio Layer III on July 14, 1995, following an internal poll. The name gave a compact identity to an audio-coding format developed largely by the Fraunhofer Society under Karlheinz Brandenburg.

MP3 reduces the data needed for a recording while aiming to retain convincing sound for listeners. Depending on bit rate, files can be around 75 to 95 percent smaller than uncompressed CD-quality audio. The codec had already been defined within MPEG-1; the familiar extension helped identify the recordings as they circulated between computers and later portable players.
